cases.description: Three sequential samples share one explicit clock and boot epoch.
A sequence gap remains explicit and is not imputed.
Out-of-order delivery is inside the declared bounded reorder window.
An exact repeated sample packet is idempotent.
A sequence is reused with a different sample identity and digest.
Sequence resets inside one boot epoch while event time continues forward.
One stream mixes samples from two boot epochs.
A monotonic clock moves backwards without a new boot epoch.
A sample uses a different timestamp basis from the stream.
A sample silently changes the time unit from seconds to milliseconds.
The stream lacks a clock-domain identity.
The stream lacks an origin for its monotonic clock.
Local wall-clock-only timestamps are not a supported ordering basis.
Clock synchronization uncertainty exceeds the declared purpose limit.
The device clock is explicitly unsynchronized.
Cross-domain mapping is required but no mapping is supplied.
A versioned clock mapping does not cover the sample time interval.
A mapping exists but its declared uncertainty exceeds the consumer limit.
Sequence width is not declared as one of the supported counter widths.
A sequence value exceeds the declared 32-bit counter range.
A counter wraps at its maximum without opening a new boot epoch.
A sample identifier is replayed with a different payload digest.
The same sequence has a different digest even though the sample ID is reused.
A sample carries a missing-as-zero payload state.
A firmware digest changes in the middle of one stream.
A configuration digest changes without a new stream identity.
Acquisition time precedes event time without a declared buffering model.
A sample has no collector receipt time.
Two packets claim the same transport-order slot.
The reordered sample arrives beyond the maximum reorder window.
Reordering is observed while the consumer policy forbids reordering.
A sequence gap occurs while the consumer policy requires complete coverage.
The declared clock source is missing.
A sample declares a different clock domain from the stream.
A sample declares a different boot epoch from the stream.
A sample is not explicitly tied to the stream clock domain.
An exact duplicate is harmless even when its collector receipt time differs.
A mapping is marked verified but has no verification receipt.
The clock mapping has been revoked after the sample interval.
Display timezone changes but the UTC/monotonic ordering identity is unchanged.
